papers.title_en: Alignment of visual brain encoding models with individual perceptual similarity judgments
papers.authors: Daniel Chong, Haomiao Chen, Keith W Jamison, Raja Marjieh, Ilia Sucholutsky, Nori Jacoby, Amy Kuceyeski
papers.evidence: 微调脑编码模型以对齐个体感知相似性判断
papers.tldr: 本研究探讨能否通过微调脑编码模型使其表征与个体感知相似性判断对齐。利用NSD数据中8名受试者对100张图像的相似性判断，将通用模型DreamSim适配为个性化感知相似度模型，再用其对编码模型微调。结果显示基线编码器虽反映受试者内感知相似度，但缺乏受试者间相关性；个性化微调后模型最符合人类感知判断且能反映受试者间相关性，为构建个性化、人类对齐的视觉脑编码模型提供了新方法。
papers.abstract_en: Encoding models that predict brain activation responses to images have traditionally been trained to maximize accuracy when predicting observed brain data. However, their internal representations may not reflect individual human perception. In this work, we investigate whether we can fine-tune brain encoding models to better align their representations with individuals' similarity judgments. Using similarity judgments of 100 images from 8 participants in the Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), we adapt a generic human similarity judgment model (DreamSim) separately for each participant to obtain personalized perceptual similarity models. These models are then used to obtain subject-specific similarity structure across images in their encoding model training sets. We fine-tune each participant's baseline encoder in two conditions, aligning its representations with either generic or personalized similarity judgments, with the same initialization and objective. We find that baseline brain encoders reflect within-subject perceptual similarity more strongly than measured fMRI responses and preserve intersubject correlations present in measured fMRI, but fail to reflect those of human perceptual similarity judgments. Fine-tuning with generic, population-level perceptual similarity information results in better alignment with human judgments than baseline encoders, but these models still fail to capture intersubject correlations of human judgments. However, fine-tuning with personalized perceptual similarity information results in models that are the most aligned with human perceptual similarity judgments and also reflect intersubject correlations of human judgments. Our framework provides an approach for bootstrapping human similarity judgment data into more individualized, human-aligned brain encoding models of vision.

papers.title_en: Do Speech BCIs Need Larger Models? Rethinking Neural Decoding beyond Scaling
papers.authors: Zehui Feng, Weichuan Wang, Xiaohan Chen, Cuntai Guan, Ting Han
papers.evidence: 言语脑机接口从神经活动到文本的解码
papers.tldr: 语音脑机接口依赖大模型但数据稀缺噪声大且昂贵，扩展收益不明。本文提出 BEST 两阶段框架，用分层中间表示和紧凑语音导向解码器直接映射神经活动到文本，在 Brain-to-Text 基准上仅用可比方法3.85%的参数取得低词错率，揭示跨模态对齐比模型规模更关键。
papers.abstract_en: Recent speech brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) increasingly rely on large models and complex multi-stage pipelines for neural decoding. However, in speech BCI, where training data are scarce, noisy, and expensive to collect, the benefits of model scaling remain unclear. This work revisits a fundamental question: are large models truly necessary for accurate neural decoding? We propose BEST (Brain-Encoding-Speech-Text), a two-stage framework for efficient neural-to-text decoding. Instead of relying on large generative models or phoneme-centric pipelines, BEST introduces hierarchical intermediate representations and a compact speech-oriented decoder that directly maps neural activity to text. This design preserves essential structure while significantly reducing computational cost, enabling robust generalization in low-resource settings and practical deployment under constrained resources. On the Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks, BEST achieves word error rates (WERs) of 6.19% and 1.62%, respectively, using only 3.85% of the parameters required by comparable methods. Beyond these results, we provide three key insights: (1) decoder scaling yields non-monotonic gains; (2) cross-modal alignment is more critical than model size; and (3) overfitting degards sequence-level performance. Representation analysis further reveals a consistent neural-audio-text alignment pathway.

papers.title_en: GRAFT-EEG: Gauge-Aware Physical Field Transport for Cross-Dataset Motor-Imagery EEG
papers.evidence: 跨数据集运动想象脑电解码中的域自适应方法
papers.tldr: 针对跨数据集EEG解码中观测算子偏移问题，提出GRAFT-EEG，通过去除共参考规范、利用模板导联场传输原生掩模，结合源拟合频谱分类器和有界SSM残差。在五个数据集上准确率60.865%，显著优于基线，证明物理场传输可提升跨数据集泛化。
papers.abstract_en: Cross-dataset EEG decoding often treats montage, reference, and active-sensor changes as representation shift, although they also alter the observation operator. We study target-statistics-blind transfer: fitting receives no target signal, label, or empirical statistic, and electrode coordinates only instantiate a fixed prediction operator. method removes the active-set common-reference gauge and transports each native mask through a template motor leadfield. A source-fitted spectral classifier anchors the decision; a bounded state-space-model (SSM) residual is secondary. We establish restricted identifiability and an operator-perturbation bound. Across five leave-one-dataset-out targets (253 participants), dynamic method achieved 60.865% equal-target balanced accuracy versus 52.684% for strict-clean 5/5 BIOT (hierarchical difference +8.182 points; 95% CI +6.382 to +10.196; positive in every target). On four EEGPT-clean targets, the descriptive means were 61.520% and 59.057%. In four post-hoc exact same-parent tests, FULL exceeded coordinate-basis, matched-spectrum, row-shuffled, and wrong-anatomy controls by 9.959, 9.698, 11.241, and 3.985 points, respectively (all 95% CIs excluded zero; Holm-adjusted P<0.001). A separate 60-participant same-paradigm evaluation retained a positive physical-operator contrast (+4.029 points; +2.338 to +5.773), whereas dynamic--static was inconclusive; its preregistered status is partial confirmation rather than unrestricted external validation. The SSM added +1.059 points (+0.013 to +1.892). Claims remain bounded to five binary motor-imagery domains and the tested operators.

papers.title_en: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
papers.authors: Ingo Marquardt, Anthilia Alchanat, Priyanka Jain
papers.evidence: 使用LLM嵌入从EEG中解码词/段落级信息
papers.tldr: 本研究探究EEG静默阅读中语言模型各层可解码信息分布，发现词级信息集中于早期层，而段落级上下文信息随深度增强，即使单窗口解码器也能跟踪文本，且通过控制实验排除词解码和会话伪影，表明EEG携带话语级信息，目标层选择可调节语言解码。
papers.abstract_en: In a previous report we showed that a decoder can recover open-vocabulary word-level information from 19-channel EEG recorded during silent reading, by aligning short EEG windows with hidden-state embeddings of the presented word taken from a large language model (LLM). That analysis contrasted two of the model's 33 layers: the context-free input embedding and one mid-depth layer. Here we ask how EEG-decodable structure is distributed over the full depth of the language model. We trained one decoder per layer of Llama-3.1-8B, with and without a causal transformer over the sequence of EEG windows. We distinguish word-level decodability from a context-tracking component. Word-level decodability peaks in early layers and declines steadily towards the last layer. In contrast, the context-tracking component of the retrieval gain rises with depth, both with and without a causal transformer. Unexpectedly, a decoder that sees a single 0.5-s window at a time tracks the text passage too. Two new controls dissect this component. A target-geometry control, a synthetic predictor made of the true target plus noise calibrated to each decoder's word-level accuracy, shows that context tracking is not a by-product of word decoding and target geometry. A control that permutes predictions across runs from either the same or from different sessions shows that most of the observed context-tracking is not caused by an EEG recording session signature. Instead, context tracking mostly follows the text. A single EEG window therefore carries passage-level information that a contextual target can absorb. The results locate word identity in the early layers of the language model, discourse state in the deeper layers, and make the choice of target layer a design dial for EEG language decoders.

papers.title_en: TriRouter: Sparse-to-Dense Electrode-Space Routing for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding
papers.evidence: 鲁棒EEG运动想象解码用于脑机接口
papers.tldr: 针对多通道EEG运动想象解码中电极缺失问题，提出TriRouter电极空间路由框架，融合判别保持、掩码鲁棒和潜在补偿三条路径，通过验证校准路由器动态分配贡献，在BNCI2014-001及低通道数据集上显著提升稀疏/损坏电极下的解码精度，优于现有基线。
papers.abstract_en: Motor imagery brain-computer interfaces require reliable decoding from multichannel EEG, but practical acquisition often yields sparse or corrupted electrode montages. We propose TriRouter, an electrode-space routing framework with discriminative-preservation, mask-robustness, and latent-compensation paths. A validation-calibrated router uses observable channel availability to allocate path contributions, preserving complete-channel discrimination while increasing representation recovery under severe missingness. In BNCI2014-001, TriRouter outperforms standard public backbones and a dynamic-spatial-filtering corrupted-EEG baseline. It improves accuracy over the strongest corrupted-EEG baseline by 3.68, 4.02, and 6.46 percentage points at nominal 25%, 50%, and 75% missing settings, and remains effective under structured regional missingness and additional low-channel dataset evaluation.

papers.title_en: RTSM: Adapting Recursive Models to Multivariate Time-Series Classification
papers.authors: Georg Tenzing, Anna Tegon, Luca Benini, Thorir Mar Ingolfsson
papers.evidence: 用于解码时序模式的多元时间序列分类
papers.tldr: 针对多元时间序列分类，本文提出递归时间序列模型（RTSM），通过权重绑定细化避免逐层新增参数，并重点关注时间表示与潜在状态组织。模型结合学习型卷积时间分词器、单状态权重绑定细化模块和池化分类读出。在30个UEA数据集上取得17个深度学习模型中最高的72.81%平均准确率，比MambaSL高1.60个百分点，验证了设计选择的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Accurate multivariate time-series classification requires extracting temporal features and integrating information across a sequence. Weight-tied refinement offers a way to repeatedly process these features without allocating new parameters at each stage. Applying this principle to time series requires choosing both a temporal representation and a latent-state organization suited to classification. We introduce the Recursive Time-Series Model (RTSM), which combines a learned convolutional temporal tokenizer, single-state weight-tied refinement, and a pooled classification readout. Across all 30 UEA datasets, RTSM achieves 72.81% mean accuracy under validation-based configuration and checkpoint selection, the highest observed mean among the 17 evaluated deep-learning models and 1.60 percentage points above MambaSL. Ablations on eight datasets favor the proposed tokenizer over a simple convolutional embedding and the single-state model over the tested two-state variants. The complete classifier reaches 86.10% mean accuracy versus 84.79% for a separately trained tokenizer-only classifier. These findings identify temporal encoding and state organization as key design choices for adapting recursive architectures to time series. The resulting classifier combines competitive accuracy with a shared refinement module whose parameter count is independent of computational depth.
